title: Alleged co-conspirator in Tumbler Ridge shooting has trial delayed until December 2027

blocks.text: British Columbia·New

The trial for alleged Tumbler Ridge shooting co-conspirator Melody Bryant has been delayed from next month to December 2027 after she waived her right to a speedy trial and requested more time to review the discovery materials.
Melody Bryant, 30, is charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country
· CBC News
· Posted: Nov 19, 2026 3:08 PM EST | Last Updated: 22 minutes ago
The alleged co-conspirator in the deadly mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C., has had her trial delayed until December 2027.

Washington state resident Melody Bryant, 30, is charged with conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country, an offence that carries a maximum sentence of life in prison and a $250,000 fine. She has pleaded not guilty.

A Seattle grand jury indicted Bryant in October and a trial was originally supposed to begin next month, on Dec. 21, but Bryant waived her right to a speedy trial on Nov. 10 and asked for more time to review the "tens of thousands of electronic communications and numerous law enforcement reports" from both the FBI and RCMP in order to prepare.
The court agreed, and the trial is now scheduled to begin on Dec. 6, 2027, but could be delayed up to Jan. 10, 2028.
Accused Tumbler Ridge co-conspirator enters not guilty plea in U.S. court

Bryant, who was originally identified by law enforcement as James Cody Bryant but who is named as Melody in the courts, is accused of helping 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar plan her attack in Tumbler Ridge.

blocks.text: On Feb. 11, Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother Jennifer Strang, 39, and half-brother Emmett Jacobs, 11, in their home. She then drove to Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and gunned down Abel Mwansa, 12, Zoey Benoit, 12, Ezekiel Schofield, 13, Kylie Smith, 12, Ticaria Lampert, 12, and educational assistant Shannda Aviugana-Durand, 29.

Eight people were killed in the Feb. 10, 2026, mass shooting in Tumbler Ridge, including five children, an educational assistant, and the shooter's mother and half-brother, both pictured bottom right. (CBC News)

An RCMP investigation revealed the shooter had started a livestream on the social media platform Twitch as she was headed to the school. The stream lasted just 20 seconds and showed her sitting in a vehicle with a long gun and rifle in her lap. It was watched by one account, which belonged to Bryant, according to the FBI.
Bryant and the shooter had been chatting on a messaging app called Discord for months. When Mounties learned Bryant was a resident of Bellingham, Wash., they notified the FBI.
Law enforcement have laid out chat logs between Bryant and Van Rootselaar in which Bryant is alleged to have given tactical advice and financial support in advance of the shooting.
Cross-border testimony cited as challenge
The cross-border nature of the investigation, with Bryant in the United States and the actual crime in Canada, is one of the challenges of the trial.

The defence motion notes that beyond what has already been disclosed, the prosecution is awaiting "additional voluminous discovery materials" from the RCMP, "including expert reports regarding crime scene analysis." The filing adds that the case will involve cross-border testimony from Canadian witnesses and "other foreign evidence."

Bryant is being held at a federal detention centre in Washington state referred to as SeaTac where she will only be allowed to review materials in a controlled environment, with no ability to print or copy materials, or upload them into AI tools "where rights to the data are retained by any party that has not explicitly agreed to be covered by the protective order."
